contexts.text: It is known that a person is drawn to his own way of thinking...
A sentence by the religiosity in which was the Jewish nation. Signified.
A milder sentence. Signified. AC 5761. AC 5762.
Nor were they indignant if one did not accede to the way of thinking of another.

For he who defends his opinion against others who attack it, confirms himself more in his own opinion, and also then finds many things confirmatory of his opinion which he before had not noticed, and many things which deny the opposite one; and thus he becomes firmer in his opinion, and also illustrates it by many things.
Under Opinion, see this reference.
To answer = to give sentence, and judge.
I will add this angelic deliverance...
These have one mind () = that they acknowledge unanimously. ( = unanimity. AE 1071.)
God hath put into their hearts to do His mind, and to do one mind () = judgment with them from the Lord... and a unanimous judgment... AE 1084.
Conjoin these three into one sentence. CL 136.
After the judgments, they carried out the verdicts.
I asked them to write some sentence on a paper...
My verdict is... TCR 459:5. TCR 459:6. etc.
A judge, when he has heard the evidence... produces his verdict, and pronounces judgment.

That the faith... makes the sentence: if true faith conjoins itself with good, sentence is made for eternal life; but if faith conjoins itself with evil, sentence is made for eternal death. General article.
The opinion now flourishing in the Churches is...
He thought against my way of thinking.
They who have studied faith (always) remain in their own way of thinking...
Charles XII never wanted to desist from his purpose... He could confirm his obstinate purpose by such things as did not appear to be evil. (Two examples given of these evil purposes of his.)
When they are in an opposite opinion, they vanish; and those are suddenly present who are in a like opinion.
As soon as a Spirit dissents in opinion from another, he disappears.
He wanted to know whether such was their doctrine and way of thinking.
